public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs cannot be trusted to run anything on their own.

statement.excerpt: LLMs are sold as “AI,” a technology best-known for automating things, yet they can’t be trusted to run anything on their own.

from_speaker: to run anything on their own
our_interpretation: The plain reading is a universal claim about practical autonomous operation, not a requirement that software never make an error.
A counterexample must reliably execute a defined workflow without case-by-case human approval or correction. Ordinary setup, maintenance and monitoring are allowed.
Marketing a workflow as automated or recording unanswered conversations as resolved does not itself establish reliability.
For this ongoing capability observation, use May 2026, the latest complete month before the post. No reporting cadence is specified, so this period choice is an evaluator interpretation.
criteria.support_condition: Broad operational evidence establishes that no relevant class of defined LLM workflow meets a reasonable task-specific reliability standard without case-by-case human supervision.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one production workflow in the target period demonstrably operates without case-by-case human supervision and meets a documented, task-appropriate standard for successful completion and errors.
